assessment.nobel_worthiness: A new door in the sense I value most: tuning a single materials parameter, the twist angle, produces flat bands, correlated insulators and superconductivity in a clean, reproducible platform. The 2018 transport experiments were the original observation and the field they opened (moire quantum matter, fractional Chern states) is large and still growing.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald predicted the magic angle and flat band in 2011; Jarillo-Herrero's group made the decisive 2018 experimental observation. That is a clean theory-plus-original-experiment configuration. Cao and other co-authors, and the Dean and Young groups on hBN-encapsulated devices, are outside the credited list and the experimental split deserves scrutiny.
assessment.maturity: Independently reproduced by many groups with direct spectroscopy (STM, nanoSQUID) and by transport; the core phenomena are stable. The superconducting mechanism is still debated, so recognition rests on the discovery of the platform rather than on a settled interpretation. Arguably slightly early but not premature.
uncertainties: Whether the prize should credit the superconductivity and correlated insulator discovery as one compound achievement or also acknowledge parallel work on other moire systems.
Disputed or incomplete allocation between the experimental team members; I am relying on memory for author lists and have not verified them.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: A genuine invention: a laser whose wavelength is set by layer thickness in a semiconductor heterostructure rather than by the bandgap, demonstrated in 1994 and now a workhorse for mid-infrared spectroscopy, gas sensing and security. The device worked as an instrument from the beginning and has verified impact for science and society.
assessment.attribution: The 1994 demonstration was by Faist, Capasso and colleagues at Bell Labs; Capasso led the concept and Faist did much of the hands-on realization. Cho supplied the MBE growth capability, which was essential but is closer to enabling technology, and the Bell Labs team included others such as Sirtori and Sivco who are not credited here. I propose two names, the conceptual and experimental originators, while noting Cho as the third option.
assessment.maturity: Mature: three decades of continuous-wave, room-temperature operation, commercial products and independent groups. Recognition is overdue rather than premature.
uncertainties: Whether Cho's growth contribution outweighs that of other Bell Labs co-inventors.
Earlier proposals of superlattice intersubband lasing (Kazarinov and Suris, 1971) complicate the historical record of the original idea and I cannot verify the priority claims.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical lattice clocks reached fractional uncertainties near 1e-18 and thereby enabled tests of fundamental constants, relativistic redshift at the millimetre scale and a path to redefining the second. The measurements are unambiguous, quantitative and verifiable, exactly what I trust.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice concept and made the first Sr clock; Ye's group brought the clock to record accuracy and stability. Two laureates fits cleanly. Others such as Hall and Hansch (already recognized for the comb) and Lemonde/Takamoto groups contributed, but the central credit is clear.
assessment.maturity: Several independent clocks (Sr, Yb) agree at the 1e-18 level and international comparisons exist. The technology is still evolving toward redefinition of the SI second, which is a downstream outcome rather than a requirement for the discovery.
uncertainties: Part of the field's impact lies ahead (redefinition of the second, geodesy), so timing could be argued either way.
Overlap with earlier Nobel recognition of frequency combs and ion-trap clocks may be raised as incremental.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Room-temperature tunnel magnetoresistance in 1995 was the original discovery that made magnetic tunnel junctions useful, and the MgO-barrier giant TMR then enabled hard-disk read heads and MRAM. It follows the 2007 GMR prize logically and has very large documented technological impact.
assessment.attribution: Miyazaki and Moodera independently reported large room-temperature TMR in 1995 and are the original discoverers. Parkin and Yuasa/Djayaprawira (Canon-Anelva, AIST) reported the coherent-tunnelling MgO enhancement in 2004; Parkin's credit is for the MgO step and for broader spintronic engineering. Julliere's 1975 low-temperature observation complicates priority, and Yuasa is not in the supplied credit list.
assessment.maturity: Fully mature with products in the field for nearly two decades. Possibly overshadowed by the 2007 prize, which committee members may see as having covered spintronics.
uncertainties: Priority issue with Julliere (1975) and with the split between the 1995 discovery and the 2004 MgO enhancement, which may need different recipients.
Whether the 2007 GMR prize makes this seem incremental.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The 2012 observation of a Higgs-like boson was an experimental discovery of the first order, built on instruments of unprecedented scale and reproducibility. It completed the Standard Model and verified a decades-old prediction, which the 2013 prize already recognized on the theory side.
assessment.attribution: Credit for a collaboration of thousands is the difficulty. The names supplied are the conceivers and long-time leaders of ATLAS and CMS, which gives an invention-of-the-instrument rationale, but the physics statutes require a discovery or invention by identifiable people and the committee has historically hesitated here. Individual contributions to the actual discovery analyses are not captured by these three names.
assessment.maturity: Thoroughly confirmed by two independent experiments and subsequent coupling measurements; the interpretation is stable. Timing is not an issue except the question of why the experiments were not recognized in 2013.
uncertainties: Whether the statutes and committee practice allow an experimental prize for detector conception and leadership.
Fair allocation within ATLAS and CMS is inherently unresolved and I am not able to verify who played the decisive analysis roles.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ti:sapphire provided a broadband, solid-state gain medium and mode-locking (Kerr-lens, then SESAMs) turned it into a practical femtosecond source underpinning ultrafast spectroscopy, microscopy and attosecond science. This links directly to physics the committee honoured in 2023 and 2018 and is a clear instrument-driven door-opener.
assessment.attribution: Moulton demonstrated the Ti:sapphire laser at MIT Lincoln Lab (1982); Keller invented the semiconductor saturable absorber mirror enabling robust passive mode-locking. Sibbett's group demonstrated Kerr-lens mode-locking with Spence and Sibbett in 1991, whose priority relationships with other discoverers are not entirely clear to me. I propose Moulton and Keller as the two clearest originators and note the Kerr-lens point as an unresolved allocation. Recognizing Keller would also be welcome for diversity, though that is not a criterion by itself.
assessment.maturity: Mature, with decades of widespread use. Impact is demonstrated by commercial systems and countless downstream experiments.
uncertainties: Attribution between Kerr-lens mode-locking (Sibbett and colleagues) and SESAM work (Keller) is a compound discovery that may need separate recognition.
Possible concern that this overlaps with chirped-pulse amplification and attosecond prizes.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical detection of a single nitrogen-vacancy centre in 1997 and the demonstration of coherent control at room temperature opened an atomic-scale sensing platform that can image magnetic fields, temperature and spins in cells and materials. This is a tool that lets people see what they could not see before, which appeals to me as a microscopist.
assessment.attribution: Gruber, Wrachtrup, Jelezko and colleagues made the original single-NV observation and the early coherent control. Lukin's group contributed major later developments in sensing, quantum registers and entanglement, but the original experimental discovery points to Wrachtrup and Jelezko. Related credit also belongs to the Hanson group in a different ballot entry, which suggests overlapping configurations.
assessment.maturity: Replicated worldwide with many sensing applications, but many of the promised practical uses (nanoscale NMR, in-cell sensing) are still developing, so impact is partly prospective.
uncertainties: Overlap with the optical-spin-interface entry for quantum networks; I cannot determine which framing the committee should prefer.
Maturity of applications is uneven and I have not verified the state of in-vivo sensing claims.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Multiferroics combine ferroelectricity and magnetism and the combination of first-principles design (Spaldin) with epitaxial BiFeO3 films (Ramesh) and discovery of strong magnetoelectric control in TbMnO3 (Tokura and colleagues) gave a new materials design principle. As an electron microscopist I know how crucial atomic-scale interface characterization has been to this field.
assessment.attribution: The three names correspond to distinct roles: theory and design, thin-film realization, and bulk discovery of strong cross-coupling. These are three separate contributions rather than one decisive experiment, so the allocation is plausible but not obvious; Kimura's TbMnO3 work, Wang et al., and Schmid's terminology are not credited.
assessment.maturity: The material class is well established, but technological application (low-power magnetoelectric memory) has not yet been demonstrated at scale, and the central claim is of broad influence rather than a single verified discovery. I regard this as the most uncertain of my eight in maturity.
uncertainties: Compound discovery with weakly connected parts; the original experiment is not clearly one event.
Practical benefit not yet proven; may be premature.
